scenes.result: Learned finished 7.13 bps worse than Urgency

about: Two simulated traders work the same order on the same simulated market. To rest is to wait in the queue for a better price, and to cross is to pay the spread and fill now.
The learned policy uses a fill model to price both choices at every decision, and the urgency rule rests until it falls more than 30 lots behind an even schedule.

Playback runs at four times simulated speed and stops wherever one trader rests while the other crosses. Trades land at their recorded times, the book updates once a second as it was recorded, and a negative cost means the fills beat the price at arrival.
verdict: The learned policy passed the rule frozen before the test. It saved 0.064 bps per order (95% interval 0.014 to 0.110), resampling 34 days against the urgency rule, with a smaller tail and far less forced completion.

results.name: Frozen rule
results.scope: Learned policy against the urgency rule on 909 paired simulated orders over 34 test days.

results.name: Mean cost
results.scope: 95% interval 0.014 to 0.110 bps, resampling whole days, against the urgency rule.

results.name: Forced lots
results.scope: Share of lots finished by the deadline rule, against the urgency rule on the same orders.

results.name: 95th percentile cost
results.scope: Against the urgency rule on the same orders.

results.name: Crossing at once
results.scope: Mean cost of the learned policy against immediate crossing, 95% interval 1.97 to 5.69 bps.

results.name: Replay speed
results.scope: The C book on one core, best of 15 runs on a shared machine, 7.8x the Python reference.

results.name: Fuzzing
results.scope: C against the Python reference in 100,000 cases under AddressSanitizer and UBSan.

results.name: Tests
results.scope: 99% line coverage of the engine and 81% of the package when the study was recorded.

strategies.scope: Mean and 95th percentile cost in bps on 909 paired simulated orders over 34 test days, with the share of lots forced at the deadline. Positive numbers are costs.

failed: With a 10% participation cap the result reverses, and the learned policy averages +0.028 bps with a 95% interval of +0.011 to +0.045 against the urgency rule.
With 250 ms of added latency the interval reaches zero, at −0.073 bps with a 95% interval of −0.135 to +0.016 against the urgency rule.
With 50 ms of added latency the interval reaches zero, at −0.065 bps with a 95% interval of −0.123 to +0.007 against the urgency rule.
The other 15 of 18 moved assumptions left the conclusion in place.
On the 6 sparse test days the difference is unclear, at +0.060 bps with a 95% interval of −0.065 to +0.228.
The fitted Q comparator lost clearly, at +1.17 bps with 19.6% of lots forced, and it had no tuning of its own.
limits: The feed is fixed, so a simulated order never moves a price and nobody reacts to it.
The feed is a seeded synthetic market whose signal strength was set by this project, so none of this shows what a real venue would pay.
Sparse synthetic days can show spreads of 50 ticks, far wider than normal, so the largest gains and losses here are not realistic.
Fills come from a queue model, and the stress tests show how much the answer depends on it.
